texts: No, no, no... lol, we're not going comprehensive here. Remixing is what got me into music and I've been slicing up songs as far back as 1998. So no, this list won't be comprehensive. Just some of the best. Not only that, but even me... _I_ don't remember all my remixes. And I have a hell of a memory. Then every few years, a fan will post a copy of one they liked that I'd forgotten, like my remix of "Banged and Blown Through" (NIN) that my friend Lita posted two years ago [here on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7gCvdAuLwsg). I'd completely forgotten that one. But these here below are fan favorites that _have_ to be included.

content.text:
## Moby - The Sky Is Broken (Jaya Prime's 3am Mod)

My absolute favorite piece of the original track was always those crescendo waves of simple notes washing out over the end just like waves on the ocean. Over the years, I started sampling that exact progression, bleeding it in earlier and earlier during my "[Blood of the Moon](blood-of-the-moon)" DJ sets until it finally mutated into this definitive 3am trip-hop mod. I love that instead of hunting down a traditional vocalist, Moby just went straight in with spoken, freeform poetry. That raw delivery was actually one of the earliest inspirations that pushed me to start wiring my own poetry directly into my music.

## The Glitch Mob - Drive It Like You Stole It (Jaya Prime's Rechill)

I was out there in the trenches right from the jump -- from edIT's OG solo drops to Ooah's very first singles. I was physically there at Burning Man when they had to literally stop Kraddy and cut the sound entirely because our dancing was shaking the dome so violently it was about to collapse the whole structure right on top of us. That was the legendary night _"Android Porn"_ ([Spotify](https://open.spotify.com/album/4kz2dOVi4JyyM6eeUGjPJa?si=s_oXi4V2Rf6CqpWKAo-CIg)) got officially classified under BRC's "weapon of mass destruction" category.

I've survived more than ten concerts with The Mob in one incarnation or another. While some of the newer fans might turn their noses up at my heavily slowed-down, chilled-out remix, it's a direct, unapologetic callback to the gritty early IDM glitchworks that forged their name in the first place.

\[[Download on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/remixes-and-mashups)\]

content.text:
## Fractal Sky - LASER99 (Jaya Prime's 2999 RMX)

One of my many collaborations with Fractal Sky (aka, "Aaron Spence"), and with so many visual and audio collabs between us, I've written an entire page on [Fractal Sky](#?/fractal-sky). This glitch-hop remix I made of "LASER99" first debuted at The Intentheon and with Camp Mystic at Burning Man. I always planned on going back and adding a longer crescendo in the very middle, with a slight variation in wording right as the music broke and before the bass returned. Maybe one day it'll happen.

  

A few parts were easily inspired by Kraddy's "Android Porn", but really the main inspiration is from the Fractal Sky himself, who's glitchy hip-hop cuts keep pulling me back to his music time and again. The Sky continues to release hard-bass bangers year after year and didn't let the pandemic slow him down even a little. Mad respect hermano!

  

\[[Download on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/track/laser99-jaya-primes-2999-rmx)\]

## 65daysofstatic - Crash Tactics (N.L.E. by Jaya Prime)

Anyone who got hooked on my Daft Punk "[TH3 GR1D](daft-punk-the-grid-remix)" remix is going to completely devour this frenetic, glitched-out, "Near-Life Experience" retake of the post-rock classic "Crash Tactics." I don't just love this mix -- writing this here in 2026, the apocalyptic lore behind the band's name hits harder and feels more terrifyingly relevant than ever.

It's rooted in two ideas: that sixty-five days of pure static and dead communications is all it takes to violently overthrow an entire country -- or, in the case of a rogue AI, shutting down GPS, the internet, radio, and TV for just over two months to hijack the globe. That... and sixty-five days of unrelenting static noise is the exact timeframe required to drive a single human creature completely, irredeemably insane.

\[[Download on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/remixes-and-mashups)\]

## Nine Inch Nails - Discipline (Bound by Jaya Prime)

Let's get one thing completely straight: this remix was forged for one very specific, batshit crazy, intensely violent, flawfully beautiful, and incredibly dangerous woman who I love the goddamned hell out of! You know exactly who you are. The fact that the rest of the world caught onto the remix and kept reposting it over the years? That's just a secondary, accidental byproduct. It was never the goal. I have this lethal fascination with danger -- bordering on a straight-up addiction -- that constantly drags me headfirst into train wrecks and lost causes. If I didn't strap on a safety belt every now and then, this life would've violently flatlined me years ago.

It probably still will.

\[[Download on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/remixes-and-mashups)\]

## Graeme Revell - Pain and Retribution (Limitless Remix by Jaya Prime)

The original script, the haunting soundtrack, and the raw celluloid of _The Crow_ stand as an absolute, untouchable cornerstone of the 90s. T-Bird's final words permanently scarred me -- the sheer, abject terror bleeding out of him as the realization finally took hold, and the choked way those words escaped his throat. My sister Gaea said it best, _"We're right there with him. We feel the realization and the horror in his voice and in his eyes."_

For me, this was the absolute final remix I cut before stepping away and retiring from production in 2014. Honestly? I probably shouldn't've even touched this one. Definitely not with all those chaotic glitch elements, and definitely not with how violently I tore the original to pieces. But since it marks the dying breath of that era, I'm bringing it to you exactly as it is: in the scarred, deeply imperfect form I originally released it in.

\[[Download on Bandcamp](https://sanjayaprime.bandcamp.com/album/remixes-and-mashups)\]

## Extended Exploration

If you somehow missed them, my multi-award-winning remix of "[The Grid](daft-punk-the-grid-remix)" by Daft Punk better already be on your radar. For fans of my emotional and deeper songs, my remix of "[A Drowning](a-drowning-remix)" by How to Destroy Angels is waiting for you. And to Nikki, my fallen angel, you know it goes out to you and LiLi especially. Then for the epic remix for fans of the _Aliens_ franchise, don't miss my viral "[Last Memory of Fire](last-memory-of-fire)" remix or hear it in our "[Warriors in Waiting](warriors-in-waiting-live-set)" live set.
